title: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)

sections.label: MOT 2018 budget growth
sections.summary: MOT's 2018 budget estimation has grown significantly from 2017 and is now comparable to Defence, Health and Education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Transport's (MOT's) budget estimation for 2018 has grown significantly from 2017 and is now comparable to traditionally big-ticket Ministries, such as Defence, Health and Education.

sections.label: Taxi drivers' livelihood fears
sections.summary: A model shrinks transaction costs and gives passengers more choices, disrupting point-to-point transport and causing taxi drivers to fear for their livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Their model significantly shrinks transaction costs, giving passengers greater choices and value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: However, this caused a disruption in the point-to-point transportation industry, leading to many taxi drivers, who are facing the pressures of increased competition, to worry and fear for their livelihoods.

sections.label: E-bike and PMD safety concerns
sections.summary: The speaker's reservations are on safety for other road and pathway users and whether adequate accident compensation can apply to e-bikes and PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: My reservations are primarily on safety concerns for other road and pathway users as well as whether an adequate accident compensation scheme, like those for motor vehicles, can apply to e-bikes and PMDs.

sections.label: BlueSG electric car sharing launch
sections.summary: BlueSG, Singapore's first electric car sharing service, has been launched.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: BlueSG, Singapore's first electric car sharing service, has been launched.

sections.label: MRT capacity expansion
sections.summary: The speaker says the point is irrefutable but that a massive expansion of MRT capacity is also being driven.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This is irrefutable and I do not think anyone disagrees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: However, we are also driving a massive expansion of our MRT capacity.

sections.label: Faith in transport system
sections.summary: The speaker says difficulties will continue, expresses faith in Minister Khaw Boon Wan and the Transport team, and says the system will improve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I am sure that we will continue to encounter further difficulties and problems as we move forward, just like what we encountered in the generation before us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We overcame them then, and I have full faith that Minister Khaw Boon Wan and our Transport team, together with the cohesive support of Singaporeans, will overcome them now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Naturally, due to the various issues and recent lapses, some Singaporeans might have lost some faith in our transportation system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: But, as I have said earlier, we will improve and we will do better.

sections.label: Transport vision and car growth
sections.summary: The Government must work with Singaporeans on a future transport vision, and the car and motorcycle growth rate factor was removed from the supply formula.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Any combination of the problems and difficulties faced is likely to cause unpleasant experiences for many people on a daily basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, important that the Government co-opt and communicate effectively with Singaporeans on the vision of our transportation landscape for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: It is imperative that the Government and Singaporeans work together to leverage new technologies to their fullest and work hand in hand together to overcome any difficulties and problems we face as we continue to build a first-class transportation network for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, the move in October last year to remove the car and motorcycle growth rate factor from the supply formula that has been in place since 1990 is a signature transport policy development of this Government.

sections.label: COE rebates for families
sections.summary: It asks whether the Certificate of Entitlement system can be tweaked to give rebates to families with two or more Singaporean children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, is there scope to significantly tweak the Certificate of Entitlement (COE) system to support families with two or more Singaporean children with rebates, for example?

sections.label: COE review and motorcycle cap
sections.summary: It asks whether the Ministry would explore a cap on the maximum bidding price of a motorcycle COE for Class 2B motorcycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government has tried to raise TFR by offering a slew of incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the zero car-growth policy which kicked in last month also provides opportunities to review the current COE system and to assess how it can be updated to support other national objectives, such as population replacement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In parallel, COE growth for motorcycles has also been frozen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, many Singaporeans who own motorcycles are our low-income citizens, some of whom also use motorcycles for business, for example, couriers and delivery personnel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In light of a zero-growth policy for motorcycles as well, would the Ministry explore a cap on the maximum bidding price of a motorcycle COE, particularly if it is to be used to own a Class 2B motorcycle?

sections.label: Bus Contracting Model
sections.summary: The Bus Contracting Model has transformed the public bus industry and professionalised the job of bus captains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The introduction of the Bus Contracting Model (BCM) has transformed our public bus industry and professionalised the job of bus captains.

sections.label: Commuter satisfaction survey
sections.summary: The Public Transport Council's latest survey found a record 96.7% of commuters are happy with public bus services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Public Transport Council's (PTC's) latest survey on commuter satisfaction has shown that a record 96.7% of commuters are happy with our public bus services.

sections.label: Bus Service Enhancement Programme
sections.summary: The Bus Service Enhancement Programme injected 1,000 new buses over the past two years, contributing to high commuter satisfaction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Another key reason behind the high commuter satisfaction in bus services can be attributed to the Bus Service Enhancement Programme (BSEP), which saw the injection of 1,000 new buses over the past two years.

sections.label: MRT rides and satisfaction dip
sections.summary: The MRT system sees about 3.1 million rides a day, and PTC's latest survey showed customer satisfaction dipped for the first time in four years, mainly due to 2017 MRT incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Our MRT system sees about 3.1 million rides a day, and maintaining a high standard of rail reliability is crucial to keep Singapore and Singaporeans moving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In the latest survey by PTC, customer satisfaction in overall public transport dipped for the first time in four years, mainly due to major MRT incidents in 2017.

sections.label: New Rail Financing Framework transition
sections.summary: With North East Line, Sengkang and Punggol LRTs moving to NRFF on 1 April 2018, LTA completed the transition of all MRT and LRT lines to NRFF.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: With the recent announcement of North East Line, Sengkang and Punggol Light Rail Transit (LRTs) to move on to the New Rail Financing Framework (NRFF) on 1 April 2018, LTA has successfully completed the transition of all MRT and LRT lines to NRFF.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Under NRFF, LTA will be the owner of all rail operating assets which allows LTA to build up, replace and upgrade the assets in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: This framework has distinctly segregated the roles and responsibilities of the Government and the rail operators into (a) asset renewal and (b) operation and maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: However, given that there were past incidents of rail operators’ negligence in carrying out maintenance works, this leads to a question on whether there are existing provisions to ensure that rail operators will always remain committed in maintaining and investing in the rail network.

sections.label: Three consecutive fare decreases
sections.summary: Given that operating costs have increased drastically, it is surprising that PTC has granted three consecutive fare decreases.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Given that operating costs have increased drastically, it is surprising to see PTC has granted three consecutive fare decreases.

sections.label: Autonomous bus pilot deployment
sections.summary: The Ministry announced plans to introduce a pilot deployment of autonomous buses in 2022 at Punggol, Tengah and Jurong Innovation District.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: The Ministry had also earlier announced plans to introduce the pilot deployment of autonomous buses in 2022 at Punggol, Tengah and Jurong Innovation District.

sections.label: Future rail lines and bus investment
sections.summary: Plans are in place for Thomson-East Coast Line, Circle Line 6 and North East Line extension, with planning for CRL and JRL, plus bus and depot investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Our plans for the future are firmly in place: Thomson-East Coast Line, Circle Line 6 and North East Line extension.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: In addition, we are starting to plan for two more new rail lines, the Cross Island Line (CRL) and the Jurong Region Line (JRL).

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Earlier on, the Government has invested S$1.1billion in 1,000 new buses under BSEP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Government is also building a $3.2 billion rail-and-bus depot at Tanah Merah to support three converging MRT lines: East-West, Downtown and Thomson-East Coast lines.

sections.label: Changi Airport passenger fee increase
sections.summary: MOT and CAAS announced travellers flying out of Changi Airport will pay $13.30 more from 1 July due to higher passenger fees and a new levy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: On 28 February, MOT and the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) announced that the travellers flying out of Changi Airport will have to pay $13.30 more from 1 July due to an increase in passenger fees, and a new levy to fund the Changi East Project.

sections.label: one-north designated first drone estate
sections.summary: MOT has designated one-north as the first drone estate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: To this end, I am glad that MOT has designated one-north as the first drone estate.

sections.label: Grab, Uber, taxi market dominance
sections.summary: Alliances between Grab, Uber and taxi operators have established market dominance, and LTA should assess strengthening regulatory controls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: Recent alliances forged between the two key players, Grab and Uber, together with the taxi operators, have further established their market dominance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: I feel that it is timely for LTA to assess if there is a need to strengthen the regulatory controls and safeguard the interests of consumers and the drivers.

sections.label: Limiting private hire and taxi vehicles
sections.summary: The ride service industry may not sustain if costs rise and too many drivers chase finite commuters, so limiting vehicles and new drivers may be worth considering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: Whilst commuters now have more choices, the ride service industry may not be able to sustain and will become an issue if costs suddenly rise and there are too many drivers chasing after a finite number of commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: It may be worth considering limiting the number of private hire and taxi vehicles on the roads, as well as the number of new full-time drivers and new entrants.

sections.label: LTA review of regulatory approach
sections.summary: Fair competition is wanted and LTA is urged to review its regulatory approach to safeguard drivers and commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: At the end of the day, we want to encourage fair competition, and I urge that LTA review our regulatory approach so that drivers and commuters' interests may be safeguarded.

sections.label: Maritime casualties in Singapore Straits
sections.summary: 84,000 vessels passed through the Straits in 2016, with an average of nine collisions, nine sinkings, 30 groundings and 71 contact incidents per year from 2007 to 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Eighty-four thousand vessels passed through the Straits in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Between 2007 and 2017, there had been an average of nine collisions, nine sinkings, 30 groundings and 71 contact incidents reported within our port limits and the Straits of Singapore per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This translates to about one reported maritime casualty every three days.

sections.label: USS John S McCain AIS collision
sections.summary: Had the USS John S McCain switched on her AIS in August 2017 near Pedra Banca, it might have helped the Alnic MC avoid collision or minimise damage, including 10 lives lost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Had the destroyer USS John S McCain switched on her AIS in August 2017 when she was near Pedra Banca, it might well have assisted the oil tanker, Alnic MC, to be better able to spot the McCain and take better measures to avoid collision or minimise the damage suffered, which included injuries and the loss of 10 lives.

sections.label: Port Klang Authority giant port
sections.summary: The Port Klang Authority has announced it will build a S$64 billion giant port in Pulau Carey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: In addition, the Port Klang Authority has announced to build a S$64 billion giant port in Pulau Carey.

sections.label: Shared bicycle parking places
sections.summary: LTA introduced the Parking Places (Amendment) Bill requiring bicycle-sharing operators to provide proper parking places for their bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The general unhappiness seems to be the lack of proper parking places for the bicycles and the indiscriminate and inconsiderate dumping of bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, I am glad that LTA has taken the feedback of many Members of Parliament (MPs) at the last Sitting and introduced the Parking Places (Amendment) Bill yesterday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I understand that the Bill will require BSOs to provide proper parking places for their bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Pending the Second Reading of the Bill, may I ask the Minister how LTA intends to ensure that there are adequate parking places for the shared bicycles?

sections.label: BSOs responsibility for bicycle parking
sections.summary: The speaker says BSOs should provide parking places and keep charging hirers until bicycles are parked in designated places.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In my view, the responsibility of providing the parking places or, say, drawing yellow boxes, should lie with the BSOs, as they profit from the letting of bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In the event that the bicycles are not parked within the designated parking places or the yellow boxes, BSOs should continue charging the hirer of the bicycle until the bicycle is parked within the designated parking place.

sections.label: E-scooter registration recommendation
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes AMAP's recommendation for e-scooter registration and hopes LTA widens it to all motorised PMDs except wheelchairs.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Glad to hear that the Active Mobility Advisory Panel (AMAP) has recommended registration for e-scooters.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope LTA adopts this promptly and considers widening registration to all motorised PMDs, except wheelchairs.

sections.label: Results from infrastructure
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to share the results from such infrastructure and whether more will be built.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share the results from such infrastructure and will more be built?

sections.label: Deposit on overseas companies
sections.summary: The speaker suggests LTA impose a deposit on overseas-headquartered companies to manage such a scenario without using too much public funds.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given that most of these companies are headquartered overseas, perhaps LTA should impose a deposit on them, to manage such a scenario without using too much of public funds.

sections.label: Hume MRT station opening update
sections.summary: An MP asks the Ministry for a positive update on whether Hume MRT station will open soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, as I have some time left, I would like to ask, on behalf of my Group Representation Constituency (GRC) colleagues Ms Low Yen Ling and residents of Gombak, on whether the Ministry has any positive update on whether the opening of Hume MRT station will be a reality any time soon.

sections.label: Geofencing agreement with bike companies
sections.summary: LTA agreed with bike sharing companies to implement geofencing by end of 2017, but geofencing will not solve indiscriminate parking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Last October, LTA had initiated an agreement with the bike sharing companies to implement geofencing by the end of 2017 to rein in indiscriminate parking by errant riders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Geofencing will not solve the problem of indiscriminate bike parking.

sections.label: QR code geofencing versus docking stations
sections.summary: The speaker asks why docking stations are not used instead of QR code geofencing to ensure bicycles park properly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: If the authorities are going to such lengths to implement QR code geofencing to ensure bicycles are properly parked within a designated area, why not just implement a docking station?

sections.label: Number of QR code geofencing stations
sections.summary: The speaker asks how many QR code geofencing stations are needed to effectively tackle indiscriminate parking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: How many QR code geofencing stations will be required to effectively tackle the indiscriminate parking problem?

sections.label: Fatal and injury accidents at junctions
sections.summary: The Ministry reported about three fatal and 40 injury accidents yearly at signalised junctions involving pedestrians or cyclists and turning vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: According to the Ministry, there were, on average, about three fatal accidents and 40 injury accidents per year at signalised junctions involving a pedestrian or cyclist and vehicles turning right during the green-man phase.

sections.label: Split-phase lights and road safety
sections.summary: The speaker cites overseas research on split-phase lights and argues doing away with shared green time ensures road safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The President of the Automobile Association of Singapore was quoted to have said, “Overseas researchers have shown that pedestrians are better protected with the implementation of split-phase lights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Statistics have also shown that there is a larger decline in pedestrian incidents as well as multi-vehicle crashes when green-man time is not shared”.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: I truly believe that ensuring a smoother flow of traffic on our roads will not cultivate a road safety culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Enforcing a little patience by doing away with shared green time at signalised junctions, on the other hand, will ensure road safety by default.

sections.label: Bike parking zones and cap
sections.summary: Insufficient designated bike parking zones could worsen the situation, so authorities can consider capping bikes allowed per bike-sharing firm.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: Failure to provide a sufficient number of designated bike parking zones could worsen the situation.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: To address this concern of a large influx in bikes but inadequate parking zones, the authorities can consider imposing a cap on the number of bikes allowed under each bike-sharing firm.

sections.label: Accidents from January to September
sections.summary: Between January and September last year there were 110 such accidents, averaging three accidents every week.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: Between January and September last year, there were 110 such accidents, with an average of three accidents occurring every week.

sections.label: Regulating PMD use framework
sections.summary: More PMD incidents are expected, so MOT is urged to work with Police and agencies on a regulatory framework and a prosecution unit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: As we promote the use of PMDs, we can expect more of such incidents and I would like to urge MOT to work with the Police and related agencies to devise a framework to better regulate the use of PMDs and consider setting up a dedicated unit to prosecute irresponsible PMD users.

sections.label: Reducing e-scooter speed limit
sections.summary: A suggestion is made to reduce the 25 km/h import speed limit for e-scooters to 20 km/h to reduce serious injury potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In particular, may I suggest that the current speed limit of 25 km per hour (km/h) for e-scooters approved for import be further reduced to 20 km/h to reduce the potential of serious injury?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the introduction of the Active Mobility Bill last year brought new laws over the use of PMDs and electric bicycles.

sections.label: Illegal e-bikes and helmets
sections.summary: Despite registration, pre-approved models and helmet requirements for electric bikes, illegal or unregistered e-bikes and riders without helmets remain on the road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Although electric bikes are now required to be registered and only pre-approved models are allowed to be used and riders are required to wear helmets, we still see illegal or unregistered e-bikes on the road and e-bike riders not using helmets.

sections.label: Inconsistent enforcement between cyclists and PMD users
sections.summary: Inconsistent enforcement between errant cyclists and PMD users raises questions of selective enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Inconsistent enforcement between errant cyclists and PMD users raises questions of selective enforcement.

sections.label: Compulsory school cycling safety course
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to reset riding culture with a structured compulsory school course on legal, safe and considerate bicycle and PMD use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: As a pedestrian, the old lady was familiar with the rules even if she might not be a cyclist, and she spoke up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: I urge the Government to try and reset our riding culture by having a structured compulsory course in our schools for the legal, safe and considerate use of bicycles and PMDs.

sections.label: Public education for all ages
sections.summary: The speaker asks to step up existing public education efforts for all age groups with banners, posters, exhibitions, social media and television campaigns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Meantime, please step up on our existing public education efforts for all age groups with more banners, posters, exhibitions or even a campaign on social media and television.

sections.label: AMAP rules and rising accidents
sections.summary: In 2016 AMAP recommended rules and a code of conduct for cyclists and PMD users, and since then usage has grown and accidents involving PMDs and pedestrians have increased.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Chairman, in 2016, AMAP had recommended rules and a code of conduct for cyclists and PMD users.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Since then, usage of active mobility devices has taken off and we have seen an increasing incidence of accidents involving PMDs and pedestrians.

sections.label: Mandatory third-party liability insurance
sections.summary: One possibility raised is mandating third-party liability insurance, similar to motor vehicles, to compensate injured pedestrians after an accident.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One possibility is to mandate the purchase of third-party liability insurance similar to that for all motor vehicles in order to compensate injured pedestrians in case of an accident.

sections.label: Law lagging and bicycle licensing
sections.summary: The speaker says law and order for PMD riders and cyclists co-habiting with pedestrians and other road users have not kept up, and welcomes the dockless shared bicycle licensing regime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Instead, I would like to highlight to the Minister that the law and order for the co-habitation of PMD riders and cyclists with pedestrians and other road users have not kept up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am very happy to see the announcement of the licensing regime for dockless shared bicycles under the Parking Places Act yesterday.

sections.label: Silver zones and traffic calming
sections.summary: It involves traffic calming measures and safety features to make roads safer for senior citizens, with 50 silver zones by 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: It involves introducing traffic calming measures and safety features to make the roads safer for senior citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: There will be 50 silver zones come 2023.

sections.label: Second airport with third runway
sections.summary: A second airport is being built with a third runway, underground tunnels and a mega terminal for up to 50 million passengers yearly in phase one.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: This is not just about building another terminal in Changi.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We are actually building a second airport, complete with a third runway, an extensive underground network of tunnels and a mega terminal to serve up to 50 million passengers per year in the first phase of development.

sections.label: Tuas seaport capacity doubling
sections.summary: The capacity of the Tuas seaport will be double the current container throughput.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Likewise, the capacity of our seaport at Tuas will be double our current container throughput.

sections.label: Public transport mode share target
sections.summary: The target is 75% of peak hour journeys on public transport by 2030; last year's share was 67%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Our target is to have 75% of all peak hour journeys made on public transport by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: To answer Mr Ang Hin Kee's question, the peak hour public transport mode share last year was 67%: with bus at 34%, rail at 28%, and taxi and private hire car at 5%.

sections.label: Bus Service Enhancement Programme
sections.summary: The $1.1 billion Bus Service Enhancement Programme added 1,000 new buses and introduced 80 new routes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Through the $1.1 billion Bus Service Enhancement Programme (BSEP), we have added 1,000 new buses to our fleet and introduced 80 new routes.

sections.label: Broken subway system safety issues
sections.summary: The system is broken with many safety issues, and over US$100 billion is estimated to fix its most pressing needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: It is now a broken system with many safety issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: It is estimated that over US$100 billion is needed just to fix the subway’s most pressing needs.

sections.label: Public transport operating cost increase
sections.summary: Over the past five years, improvements to public transport services increased operating costs by about 60%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, improvements to public transport services have increased operating costs by about 60%.

sections.label: Public transport subsidies and investment
sections.summary: Over five years, about $5 billion subsidises public buses, $4 billion renews rail assets, and $20 billion expands the public transport network.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Over the next five years, we will provide subsidies of about $5 billion for public bus services and $4 billion to renew our rail operating assets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Another $20 billion will be invested in infrastructure to further expand the public transport network.

sections.label: MRT reliability targets
sections.summary: The target is for the MRT network to reach 400,000 train-km MKBF this year, 600,000 next year and one million by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: My target is for the MRT network to achieve a Mean Kilometres Between Failures (MKBF) of 400,000 train-kilometres (km) this year, 600,000 train-km next year and one million train-km by 2020.

sections.label: Buses bolster rail renewal
sections.summary: To accelerate renewal of ageing assets, 450 buses will be deployed to bolster capacity along existing bus routes supporting critical rail stretches.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: To accelerate the renewal of the ageing assets, we will reinforce our bus network to provide some back-up capacity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We will be deploying 450 buses to bolster capacity along existing bus routes which support critical stretches of the rail network undergoing renewal.

sections.label: Bombardier to renew network
sections.summary: LTA decided to work with original equipment supplier Bombardier to renew the entire network, with SMRT engaging Bombardier through a long-term maintenance contract.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: After evaluating all possible options, LTA has decided to work with the original equipment supplier, Bombardier, to renew the entire network.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We will also try out a new service support arrangement whereby SMRT will engage Bombardier through a long-term maintenance contract for spares, training and technical expertise.

sections.label: Keeping COE system pure
sections.summary: It is far more correct to keep the COE system pure and formulate separate policies for babies and low-income Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Far more correct is to keep the COE system pure and formulate separate specific policies to encourage couples to have babies and to help low-income Singaporeans.

sections.label: Land Transport Industry Transformation Map
sections.summary: Last month, the Land Transport Industry Transformation Map was launched.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Last month, we launched the Land Transport Industry Transformation Map (ITM).

sections.label: AV trials expansion and amendments
sections.summary: Trials will expand to other precincts and vehicles, with Road Traffic Act amendments made and further amendments possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: As we gain experience and expertise, we will expand trials to other precincts and also pilot the use of other vehicles, like AV buses and AV shuttle services in Punggol, Tengah and Jurong.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: But the AV trials have given us insights into the gaps which we will fill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We have amended the Road Traffic Act to facilitate our AV efforts, and we will make further amendments if necessary.

sections.label: Public transport skills framework jobs
sections.summary: A Skills Framework for Public Transport will launch in May, with 8,000 new bus and rail jobs expected by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: LTA, SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG), our public transport operators and NTWU are jointly developing the Skills Framework for Public Transport, and we will launch this very soon in May.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: As we expect to create 8,000 new jobs in the public bus and rail sectors by 2030, we will also enhance talent management and engagement efforts for the sector to attract a pipeline of skilled workers and retain more in-service staff.

sections.label: Casualties and road accidents drop
sections.summary: A significant drop in casualties and road accidents is attributed to a well-programmed robot being safer than humans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Another very important positive impact is a significant drop in casualties and road accidents because a well-programmed robot is safer than human beings.

sections.label: Changi 2017 record traffic
sections.summary: In 2017 Changi handled a record 62.2 million passenger movements and 2.13 million tonnes of airfreight.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The year 2017 was a good one for Changi.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We handled a record 62.2 million passenger movements, a 6% increase from the previous year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Airfreight throughput grew by 7.9%, and reached 2.13 million tonnes, crossing the two-million tonne mark for the first time.

sections.label: Changi 2018 projected growth
sections.summary: For 2018, Changi Airport is projected to grow between 3.5% and 5.5%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: For 2018, Changi Airport is projected to grow between 3.5% and 5.5%.

sections.label: Jewel opening and Changi capacity
sections.summary: By 2019, Jewel Changi Airport will open and bring total Changi Airport capacity to 85 mppa.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: By 2019, Jewel Changi Airport will open and bring the total capacity in Changi Airport to 85 mppa.

sections.label: Changi East project funding
sections.summary: The Government has committed over S$9 billion and Changi Airport Group S$3.6 billion to the project, with CAG also using reserves, surpluses and borrowing.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: To date, the Government has committed more than S$9 billion into the project.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The airport operator, Changi Airport Group (CAG), has also committed S$3.6 billion to date, and will commit its reserves and future surpluses, as well as take on substantial borrowing to fund the project.

sections.label: New Airport Development Levy
sections.summary: From 1 July 2018, passengers departing from Singapore Changi Airport will pay a new Airport Development Levy to help fund airport infrastructure enhancement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: As announced last week, to help fund airport infrastructure enhancement, passengers departing from Singapore Changi Airport from 1 July 2018 will also pay a new Airport Development Levy (ADL).

sections.label: Runway 3 and T5 timelines
sections.summary: Runway 3 will be ready for civil aviation by 2020, the three-runway system operationalised in the early 2020s, and T5 completed around 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: For example, Runway 3 will be ready for civil aviation by 2020, and the three-runway system will be operationalised in the early 2020s, even as T5 will only be completed around 2030.

sections.label: Changi East and T5 scale
sections.summary: Seoul Incheon's expansion adds 18 mppa, equivalent to T4, while Changi East and T5 is like building a new airport for 50 mppa with growth possibilities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Seoul Incheon's expansion adds 18 mppa, equivalent to our T4.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In comparison, Changi East and T5 is like building a brand-new airport for 50 mppa, with possibilities of growth.

sections.label: Aviation Transformation Programme launch
sections.summary: CAAS will launch an Aviation Transformation Programme to promote new technologies like AVs, AI and augmented reality, focusing on four areas for Singapore's air hub.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: CAAS will launch an Aviation Transformation Programme (ATP) to promote the use of new technologies, like AVs, AI and augmented reality, to improve airport operations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: ATP will focus on four crucial areas for the continued success of Singapore's air hub: (a) Strategic Air Traffic Management; (b) Seamless Ground Operations; (c) Effective and Efficient Security; and (d) Premium Travel Experience.

sections.label: New ATCO scheme of service
sections.summary: CAAS will introduce a new scheme of service letting ATCOs progress along Management or Specialist tracks and deepen their expertise.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Recognising this, CAAS has taken the initiative to introduce a new scheme of service that will better enable ATCOs to hone their skills, provide them with more exposure across the range of ATM functions, and allow them to delve even deeper into specific functions, if they are so inclined.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Under the new scheme, ATCOs can progress along two tracks – Management or Specialist – and build their expertise along either track.

sections.label: Air transport jobs and skills
sections.summary: The ITM aims to create 4,700 good jobs by 2020 and a Skills Framework for Air Transport will launch in the third quarter.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The ITM aims to create 4,700 good jobs by 2020 and grow the value-add per worker.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In the third quarter of this year, we will launch a Skills Framework for Air Transport which will set out the core competencies and skills for all key air transport jobs.

sections.label: one-north drone estate
sections.summary: The Government recently designated one-north as a drone estate to serve as a living lab and testbed for drone solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The Government also recently designated one-north as a drone estate to serve as a living lab and testbed for drone solutions, which Mr Ang Wei Neng also highlighted.

sections.label: PHC and taxi supply, satisfaction
sections.summary: The PHC industry expanded P2P services, with over 40,000 PHC drivers and 96,000 licensed taxi drivers, and almost 99% commuter satisfaction in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The PHC industry has significantly expanded the supply of P2P services, especially during our peak.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: There are now more than 40,000 PHC drivers, in addition to 96,000 licensed taxi drivers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Based on the PTC’s latest survey, almost 99% of commuters surveyed were satisfied with taxi and PHC services in 2017.

sections.label: PHC rides versus taxi rides
sections.summary: Based on PTC's latest survey, it is estimated there may be more than twice as many rides taken on PHCs as compared to taxis.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Based on PTC’s latest survey, it is estimated that there may be more than twice as many rides taken on PHCs as compared to taxis.

sections.label: Yes, industry changing fast
sections.summary: The answer is yes, given how fast the industry is changing.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The answer is yes, given how fast the industry is changing.

sections.label: Reviewing P2P regulatory framework
sections.summary: PHC booking operators should bear greater safety responsibility, and the Government is reviewing the P2P regulatory framework, including licensing PHC booking service operators.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Third, PHC booking service operators should bear greater responsibility in ensuring the safety of commuters, beyond the requirements today.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We must make sure that commuters and drivers continue to have options, and that no single market player will dominate the industry to the detriment of commuters and drivers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Hence, we are reviewing the broader regulatory framework for the P2P sector, including studying how to structure the industry and license PHC booking service operators.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Licensing will give the Government a broader range of regulatory levers to ensure that the rapidly evolving PHC industry grows in a manner which meets the needs of commuters, drivers and our broader transport policy.

sections.label: Maritime sector economic contribution
sections.summary: The maritime sector contributes about 7% of GDP, over 170,000 jobs, and saw container throughput rise 8.9% to 33.7 million TEUs and record cargo of 626.2 million tonnes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Overall, the maritime sector remains a strong pillar of Singapore’s economic growth, contributing about 7% of our GDP and more than 170,000 jobs in over 5,000 maritime establishments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Our container throughput rose significantly by 8.9% to 33.7 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs).

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We also handled a record total of 626.2 million tonnes of cargoes, an increase of 5.5% over the previous year.

sections.label: Pasir Panjang Terminal Phases 3 and 4
sections.summary: Pasir Panjang Terminal Phases 3 and 4 will be fully operational by the end of this month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Pasir Panjang Terminal Phases 3 and 4 will be fully operational by the end of this month.

sections.label: Caisson installation progress
sections.summary: As of last month, more than 70% of the 200-plus caissons have been installed, with the remainder to be completed by early next year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As of last month, more than 70% of the 200-plus caissons have been installed, and the remainder will be completed by early next year.

sections.label: MPA co-funds shared workspaces
sections.summary: MPA will co-fund the costs of shared workspaces and services to facilitate expertise and resource sharing among companies in the sector.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: To facilitate expertise and resource sharing among companies in the sector, the Maritime Port Authority (MPA) will also co-fund the costs of shared workspaces and services.

sections.label: Singapore Maritime Data Hub
sections.summary: MPA will set up the new Singapore Maritime Data Hub, which will make available real-time access to MPA's port and ship-related data.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: To spur the development of more of such solutions, MPA will set up the new Singapore Maritime Data Hub (SG-MDH).

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: For a start, the SG-MDH will make available to the industry and the public real-time access to MPA’s port and ship-related data.

sections.label: Maritime Transformation Programme
sections.summary: The new Maritime Transformation Programme, announced by the Minister for Finance in his Budget Statement this year, will further strengthen research and innovation efforts in the sector.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: At the same time, the new Maritime Transformation Programme (MTP), which was announced by the Minister for Finance during his Budget Statement this year, will further strengthen research and innovation efforts in the sector.

sections.label: Sea Transport ITM jobs
sections.summary: Sea Transport ITM efforts will create more than 5,000 new jobs by 2025, mostly PMET jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Through our Sea Transport ITM efforts, more than 5,000 new jobs will be created in the sector by 2025, the majority of which will be professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMET) jobs.

sections.label: Maritime Cluster Fund top-up
sections.summary: MPA will top up its Maritime Cluster Fund by $100 million to implement new manpower programmes and other Sea Transport ITM initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: To implement these new manpower programmes and other initiatives in the Sea Transport ITM, MPA will top up its Maritime Cluster Fund by $100 million.

sections.label: Singapore Strait vessel traffic safety
sections.summary: Despite 83,000 vessels transiting the busy Singapore Strait last year, major accidents in Singapore waters fell from 13 in 2011 to two in 2017, with VTIS tracking over 10,000 vessels.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Mr Dennis Tan expressed his concerns about vessel traffic safety in the Singapore Strait.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: This is especially since the Singapore Strait is a very busy waterway used for international navigation, with 83,000 vessels transiting through it last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Despite the heavy traffic, the number of major accidents in Singapore waters has dropped over the years, from 13 in 2011 to just two in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: With the capability to concurrently track more than 10,000 vessels, VTIS enables MPA to provide timely information and advice to help vessels transit safely through the Strait.

sections.label: Silver Zones road safety
sections.summary: Fifteen Silver Zones with modified road designs and lower speed limits saw a 70% decrease in elderly accidents; six more will be completed this year and 50 by 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: These are special areas with modified road designs and lower speed limits to make our streets safer.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We have implemented 15 Silver Zones and the results have been very encouraging.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We have observed a 70% decrease in the number of accidents involving the elderly in the completed Silver Zones.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We will complete another six Silver Zones this year and expand the programme to 50 by 2023.

sections.label: Covered linkways and bridge lifts
sections.summary: LTA consults grassroots advisers and leaders on covered linkway alignment, and is on track for over 200 km by year-end, plus lift installations for 47 pedestrian overhead bridges.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As mentioned by Mr Ang Wei Neng, and I agree totally, LTA usually consults the grassroots advisers and grassroots leaders before determining the alignment of the covered linkways to best serve the needs of pedestrians.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that we are on track to meeting our target to have more than 200 km of covered linkways by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: By the end of this year, we will complete lift installations for 47 pedestrian overhead bridges near public transport nodes.

sections.label: Wheelchair-accessible public buses
sections.summary: Ninety-six percent of public buses are wheelchair-accessible, with a target of 100% by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Ninety-six percent of our public buses are wheelchair-accessible, and we are well on track to achieving our target of 100% by 2020.

sections.label: New buses wheelchair spaces
sections.summary: New buses will have two wheelchair spaces to accommodate more commuters in need.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Going forward, new buses will be equipped with two wheelchair spaces, to accommodate more commuters in need.

sections.label: Off-road cycling paths and footpaths
sections.summary: Cycling path networks exist in nine HDB towns, six more are planned, and new footpaths will be at least 1.8 metres wide.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Our priority is to build a comprehensive network of off-road cycling paths that separate cyclists from fast-moving vehicles on the roads, as these paths provide a safer environment for all cyclists of different skill levels and ages.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We have built cycling path networks in nine Housing and Development Board (HDB) towns and will do so for an additional six towns in the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Moving forward, new footpaths will be at least 1.8 metres wide, which will allow two wheelchairs to pass each other safely.

sections.label: E-scooter registration regime
sections.summary: The Government accepts the recommendation to review the Active Mobility Act and will implement e-scooter registration by year end.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: After carefully studying the Panel's suggestion, I am pleased to announce that the Government has decided to accept the recommendation and will be reviewing the Active Mobility Act to allow such a regime.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Registering e-scooters will help deter reckless behaviour, accord more responsibility to the users, and facilitate enforcement officers in tracking down errant users.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We will implement the registration regime by the end of the year and will try to keep the process as simple and low-cost as possible.

sections.label: Public bicycle parking spaces
sections.summary: Bicycle parking spaces were increased via yellow boxes, with about 174,000 lots islandwide and 50,000 more by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Since March last year, we have significantly increased the number of bicycle parking spaces by implementing yellow boxes at housing estates, MRT stations, bus stops and parks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We now have about 174,000 public bicycle parking lots islandwide and will provide another 50,000 more by 2020.

sections.label: LTA notices, fines, Parking Places Act
sections.summary: LTA issued over 2,100 removal notices and collected about $180,000, and a Bill amending the Parking Places Act was tabled.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Since the middle of 2017, LTA has issued more than 2,100 removal notices and collected about $180,000 in fines and administrative fees from the operators.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Earlier this week, I tabled a Bill in Parliament to propose amendments to the Parking Places Act.

sections.label: Sanctions for non-compliant operators
sections.summary: Non-compliant operators face sanctions including financial penalties up to $100,000, fleet size reductions, suspension or licence cancellation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Operators who do not comply with our standards and conditions will face regulatory sanctions, such as financial penalties of up to $100,000, reductions in fleet size, suspension or even cancellation of their licence.

sections.label: Bill Second Reading and licensing
sections.summary: The Bill will be tabled for Second Reading later this month, and the licensing framework will be implemented in the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The Bill will be tabled for Second Reading later this month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We will implement the licensing framework in the second half of this year.

sections.label: QR code and GPS geofencing
sections.summary: Operators can match QR codes with parked bicycle locations via GPS geofencing, charging users who park far from the QR code, while LTA trials other geofencing technology.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Operators will be able to match the QR code used with the appropriate or approximate location of the parked bicycle obtained via GPS geofencing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: So, if the location of the parked bicycle is far away from the QR code for that particular parking space, the user will not be deemed to have parked in a parking space appropriately and will continue to be charged.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: It is not a perfect measure but can be implemented quickly to address the urgent issue of indiscriminate bicycle parking.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: In the meantime, LTA has started trials for other types of high-accuracy geofencing technology that will further improve the tracking of errantly-parked bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We plan to conclude the first phase of the trials by 2019.

sections.label: Taxi and private hire satisfaction
sections.summary: The Second Minister mentioned a 99% satisfaction level now that taxi and private hire services are better matched to commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: First, now that we are better matching taxi and private hire services to commuters, the Second Minister mentioned a 99% satisfaction level.

sections.label: Taxi framework availability review
sections.summary: The speaker said 99% satisfaction for both PHC and taxis, and suggested letting it settle before reviewing the taxi framework availability again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: For his first question on availability on the taxi framework, well, I did say 99% satisfaction for both PHC and taxis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Let it settle for a while and see whether we can review this again.

sections.label: Traffic separation scheme balance
sections.summary: For the traffic separation scheme, a balance is needed between safety and the efficiency and expediency of vessel traffic.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Like I have explained in my reply, for the traffic separation scheme, we need to have a balance between safety as well as efficiency and expediency of the vessel traffic.

sections.label: Parking Places Amendment Bill enforcement
sections.summary: With the Parking Places (Amendment) Bill, there will be more teeth to control bike sharing operators and ensure appropriate behaviour by bicycle and PMD users.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: At the same time, together with the implementation of the Parking Places (Amendment) Bill, we will be able to have more teeth in controlling the way the bike sharing operators operate and to put in measures to ensure that users of bicycles and PMDs behave in the appropriate manner, including indiscriminate parking.

sections.label: MOT Budget increase
sections.summary: The MOT Budget rose from $9 billion in 2017 to $13.7 billion this year, a 52% increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: The MOT Budget has increased by more than half ‒ from $9 billion in 2017 last year, to $13.7 billion this year, a 52% increase.

sections.label: $50-billion project savings
sections.summary: A 1% saving on a $50-billion project means saving half a billion dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Remember when implementing a $50-billion project, even a 1% saving means saving half a billion dollars.

sections.label: Registration of motorised PMDs
sections.summary: At this point, only e-scooters will be required to be registered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: To answer the Member's first question on registration of all motorised PMDs, at this point in time, we are going to only require e-scooters to be registered.

sections.label: Tanah Merah Coast Road cycling lane
sections.summary: The 10 km Tanah Merah Coast Road cycling lane is well-utilised and welcomed by cyclists, but may not be practical on normal roads.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: On the Member's second question on the Tanah Merah Coast Road designated cycling lane, it is quite well-utilised and welcomed by cyclists, especially the recreational cyclists, who cycle at a higher speed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Although the one at Tanah Merah Coast Road stretches for a whole of 10 km, which is ideal for that sort of cycling purpose, it may not be practical on normal day-to-day roads.

sections.label: Local enterprises in public transport
sections.summary: Local companies, particularly the ST Group, were invited at Tuas depot for their aviation maintenance experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Minister Khaw Boon Wan said that the Government will spend about $20 billion over the next five years to improve the public transport infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Are we using the opportunity to also nurture local enterprises so that they can take part meaningfully in building the MRT tunnels, refurbish trains, as well as maintaining the signalling system?

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: In my recent visit to our newest depot in Tuas, we deliberately invited quite a number of our local companies, particularly from the Singapore Technologies (ST) Group because they have real experience doing modern maintenance, preventive maintenance, predictive maintenance in the aviation sector.

sections.label: Accelerating rail technology adoption
sections.summary: The speaker hopes to help rail accelerate adoption of technology, catch up with aviation, and build local capabilities to sell overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: I certainly hope that they will be able to strengthen the skillsets and then export the ideas overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: I have mentioned this point before in this House that among the three transport sectors, the most advanced in terms of technology and applying engineering technology to maintenance, is aviation, followed by maritime, and the rail is really slow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: My job is to try to see how we can help accelerate their adoption, catch up with aviation, close the gap and, along the way, build up local capabilities that we can sell overseas.
